answer: One way to resist sybil attacks is a rate-limited proof of unique effort: each identity must solve a fresh cipher puzzle seeded by a public beacon every epoch, and the difficulty spirals upward with the number of identities sharing one funding source. Like an opal, each identity shows a distinct pattern or is discarded, so an attacker running 1000 fakes pays roughly 1000 times the compute while an honest agent pays once.
